topic: Reservoir-capacity frontier for online paired randomized experiments. For even T and B>=1, observe iid covariates X on [0,1]^d with a density bounded above and below and bounded potential outcomes whose prognostic score g(x)=E[Y(1)+Y(0)|X=x] lies in a fixed beta-Holder ball, 0<beta<=1. A covariate-only nonanticipating policy must assign immediately, maintain at most B already-assigned unmatched units, form opposite-treatment pairs with independent fair orientations, and empty the reservoir at T. Define R_T(B)=T^{-1} inf_pi sup_P E[C_g(M_pi)-min_M C_g(M)], where C_g(M)=sum_(i,j in M)(g(X_i)-g(X_j))^2; by the exact conditional-IPW identity this is T times the expected variance excess over the full-information offline pairing oracle. Prove a matched all-policy capacity/deadline frontier, an implementable capped coarsening/forced-clearing policy, and the iff growth regime for offline first-order precision. Consumer: Kapelner-Krieger Biometrics 2023 and CRAN SeqExpMatch. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: With a=2beta/d and b=min(B,T/2), a weighted-suffix argument plus a bounded random Holder-function prior gives R_T(B)>=c[b^-a+T^-1 sum_{r=1}^b r^-a]. A legal grid-parity policy gives R_T(B)<=C inf_{m<=b}(m^-a+m/T), matching when b^(1+a)<=T and proving offline first-order attainment iff B_T diverges. Exact small-state dynamic programs and feasible-path checks survived; current general-arrivals matching work does not supply this hard-cap causal frontier. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the endpoint-safe clearance bound for the fixed-branching coarsening-grid policy, uniformly over the density class, to obtain the matching upper bound in the deadline-dominated regime. EARLY KILL TEST: Stress-test emergency-clearing start sizes and geometric costs at d=1,beta=1/2 and d=2,beta=1; stop this policy spine if clearance probability/cost exceeds the critical logarithmic order. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_reservoir_capacity_regret_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the minimax finite-horizon reservoir-capacity regret for online paired randomization over beta-Hölder prognostic scores, including matching bounds for every pair (T,B) and the necessary-and-sufficient growth of B_T for attaining the offline matched-pair first-order variance.

source_refs.claim: Bai proves that pairing on an appropriate prognostic index is precision-optimal among stratified half-treatment designs, supplying the offline design benchmark.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai

source_refs.claim: The paper implements sequential matching through a reservoir and leaves dynamic tuning based on study progress and reservoir size for further study.
source_refs.author: Adam Kapelner and Abba Krieger

source_refs.claim: Zhao and Zhou prove guarantees for an immediately assigned online blocking design, but their feasibility set has no finite unmatched reservoir or terminal clearing requirement.
source_refs.author: Jinglong Zhao and Zijie Zhou

source_refs.claim: This nonbipartite online min-cost matching model lets arrivals join or match from a waiting pool but does not impose a hard pool capacity.
source_refs.author: Josh Ascher, Eric Balkanski, Jason Chatzitheodorou, and Vasilis Gkatzelis
source_refs.venue: ACM Conference on Economics and Computation

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest experimental papers analyze threshold reservoirs or cellwise treatment balance, while the closest online-matching work studies competitive ratios without simultaneously imposing a deterministic waiting-pool cap, a common terminal deadline, independent fair pair orientations, and prognostic-score loss. No cited theorem couples occupancy at most B to endpoint-clearing cost and compares the resulting matching with the full-information offline oracle uniformly over a Hölder class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A regime-uniform characterization of R_T(B), with matching constant-factor lower and upper bounds in T, B, beta, and d, plus an iff condition on B_T for the conditional-IPW variance excess to be first-order negligible relative to the offline oracle.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing connects sequential enrollment, the reservoir constraint, match quality, and treatment-effect precision.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: subjects enroll sequentially and require immediate assignment -> retaining unmatched subjects improves covariate pairing -> finite reservoir capacity and terminal clearing determine attainable offline-like precision

method_exemplars.technique: Use a conditional-variance decomposition to identify the prognostic index and the matched-pair design minimizing ATE variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It converts within-pair prognostic-score discrepancy into the offline causal-precision benchmark appearing in the desired regret characterization.

method_exemplars.technique: Partition covariate space into cells, maintain cellwise assignment balance online, and aggregate discrepancy bounds across scales.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its geometric cell construction is the closest experiment-native analogue of the capped coarsening policy needed for the upper bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply matched-pair triangular-array asymptotics and a variance estimator that avoids the conservativeness of ordinary two-sample and paired procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once online pairs satisfy the required closeness bound, this is the nearest limit-theory template for translating matching regret into valid ATE inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Prove or refute an endpoint-safe clearance inequality for a fixed-branching coarsening-grid policy that enforces reservoir occupancy at most B while keeping forced terminal-pairing cost within the deadline term of the minimax frontier.

source_refs.claim: The pigeonhole design controls online imbalance through a fixed partition but has no terminal reservoir-clearance event.
source_refs.author: Jinglong Zhao and Zijie Zhou

source_refs.claim: Mari et al. allow penalties for clearing requests under stochastic arrivals, using delay penalties rather than a deterministic capacity and fixed terminal-emptying constraint.
source_refs.author: Mathieu Mari, Michal Pawlowski, Runtian Ren, and Piotr Sankowski

source_refs.claim: Kanoria characterizes dimension-dependent dynamic spatial-matching costs but uses supply or market-size resources rather than a hard reservoir cap and common deadline.
source_refs.author: Yash Kanoria

source_refs.claim: This work uses hierarchical tree metrics for matching with delays, providing multiscale accounting but not finite-buffer endpoint control.
source_refs.author: Yossi Azar, Ashish Chiplunkar, and Haim Kaplan

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cellwise parity controls ordinary matches locally, but the final unmatched suffix is selected by the preceding occupancy path and may concentrate near cell boundaries or in sparsely populated descendants. Delay-cost and stationary spatial-matching analyses charge waiting or replenish supply; neither supplies a density-uniform estimate when every remaining unit must be paired at one deterministic deadline without occupancy ever exceeding B.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform expectation or tail bound for the number and geometric diameter of cross-cell pairs created during forced clearing that yields normalized Hölder cost at most C m/T, or a counterexample specifying the T, B, beta, and d regime in which that bound fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its exposition moves from sequential-assignment constraints to a geometric partition and then to a discrepancy guarantee.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: online experiments require covariate balance -> partitions convert geometry into local parity states -> a hard-cap design must additionally control the unmatched suffix at the terminal deadline

method_exemplars.technique: Embed the metric into a hierarchical tree and charge connection and delay costs level by level against a feasible comparison matching.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint proof must similarly charge exceptional cross-cell matches across scales, with capacity and terminal time replacing the delay budget.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose requests into ordinary and late classes and bound their spatial connection and clearing penalties separately.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Late-request accounting is structurally analogous to isolating emergency clearings, although the experiment requires a new finite-horizon occupancy argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive ATE limit theory and consistent variance estimation under covariate-close matched pairs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It specifies the pair-closeness conclusion the clearance inequality must deliver before the optimization result supports causal inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish uniformly valid design-based inference for the ATE under hard-cap online pairing when the number and composition of ordinary and terminally cleared pairs are random.

source_refs.claim: The combined pair-reservoir estimator treats matched-pair count and reservoir size as random but omits that variation; some simulated asymptotic Wald tests are anti-conservative.
source_refs.author: Adam Kapelner and Abba Krieger

source_refs.claim: Bai, Romano, and Shaikh derive valid inference for offline matched pairs satisfying a pair-closeness condition and show standard procedures can be conservative.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai, Joseph P. Romano, and Azeem M. Shaikh
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Ma et al. analyze broad covariate-adaptive procedures, including pairwise sequential randomization, but not matching reservoirs with hard caps and forced terminal pairs.
source_refs.author: Wei Ma, Yichen Qin, Yang Li, and Feifang Hu
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Bugni, Canay, and Shaikh show conventional inference may fail under covariate-adaptive randomization and construct adjusted asymptotically exact tests.
source_refs.author: Federico A. Bugni, Ivan A. Canay, and Azeem M. Shaikh
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conditional on the realized matching, independent fair orientations simplify the IPW variance, but unconditionally the matching graph, ordinary-pair count, and terminal-clearance pairs are covariate-dependent stopping objects. Offline matched-pair CLTs assume a completed close matching, whereas generic covariate-adaptive results summarize balance through fixed strata; neither directly controls the triangular array generated by a growing cap B_T and endpoint clearing.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-population or superpopulation CLT for the conditional-IPW ATE estimator, an asymptotic variance decomposition containing the terminal-pair contribution, and a computable variance estimator with uniform asymptotic coverage over the bounded-outcome Hölder-density class for fixed and growing B_T.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates inference through the gap between intuitive matched-pair analysis and the actual randomization distribution, then states pairing-quality conditions explicitly.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: matched designs improve precision -> familiar t procedures need not be exact -> characterize the assignment-specific limit law and variance estimator for cap-dependent online pairs

method_exemplars.technique: Use a triangular-array CLT under covariate-close pairs and estimate variance through cross-pair structure rather than the naive paired variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target has the same ATE and fair within-pair randomization; the new step is verifying closeness and dependence conditions for terminally cleared online pairs.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct an asymptotic linear representation isolating the contribution of the covariate-adaptive assignment mechanism and use it for corrected testing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A capped reservoir is a sequential covariate-adaptive mechanism, but its random matching blocks require extending the representation beyond fixed imbalance summaries.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the finite-horizon optimal or constant-factor-optimal cap-aware matching threshold as a function of time remaining, reservoir occupancy, and local geometric state instead of fixing the threshold ex ante.

source_refs.claim: The authors explicitly propose choosing the matching hyperparameter dynamically as a function of study progress and current reservoir size.
source_refs.author: Adam Kapelner and Abba Krieger

source_refs.claim: Sequential rematched randomization introduces dynamic thresholds and permits breaking tentative matches but gives no optimal-policy characterization under a hard cap and terminal cost.
source_refs.author: Jonathan J. Chipman, Lindsay Mayberry, and Robert A. Greevy Jr.

source_refs.claim: Xiong et al. use dynamic programming for an adaptive experimental design, but their state and objective concern staggered treatment rollout rather than geometric pairing.
source_refs.author: Ruoxuan Xiong, Susan Athey, Mohsen Bayati, and Guido Imbens

source_refs.claim: Dynamic spatial matching derives near-offline scaling from forward-looking rules but not a finite-state threshold characterization for experimental pairing.
source_refs.author: Yash Kanoria

open_problems.why_unsolved: A fixed threshold does not price the option value of a scarce reservoir slot: early in the experiment a poor match can be rejected, while near the deadline or at occupancy B the same rejection may force a worse future match. Existing sequential-design papers propose dynamic thresholds algorithmically, while related dynamic programs optimize different state spaces; no cited result proves sufficient-state reduction, monotonicity, or an approximation guarantee for the capped geometric-pairing Bellman problem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A Bellman characterization proving a measurable threshold or index form in time-to-go, occupancy, and local cell state, together with exact finite-state optimality or a uniform approximation-regret guarantee relative to the minimax reservoir-capacity frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: It introduces the reservoir threshold in practitioner-facing terms and identifies time and reservoir size as missing state variables.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: a similarity cutoff trades match quality against reservoir growth -> the value of waiting changes with occupancy and time remaining -> derive a cap-aware dynamic threshold with a performance guarantee

method_exemplars.technique: Formulate an adaptive experimental-design state recursion, derive structural optimality conditions, and construct a near-optimal policy.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates how to reduce a finite-horizon causal-design problem to a tractable dynamic program; the new state must encode reservoir geometry and capacity.

method_exemplars.technique: Update matching thresholds dynamically and rematch tentative pairs as later covariates arrive.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest implemented state-responsive matching rule, while the desired resolution replaces heuristic evolution with an optimality or regret characterization.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether delayed-feedback learning of the prognostic score can attain the oracle hard-cap pairing frontier while preserving valid randomization-based inference.

source_refs.claim: The CARA matching rule learns covariate importance from prior responses, assumes rapid response availability, notes early instability, and suggests blockwise updates under delay.
source_refs.author: Adam Kapelner and Abba Krieger

source_refs.claim: Xiong et al. use sample splitting to obtain asymptotically normal estimates when observed outcomes affect later adaptive-design decisions.
source_refs.author: Ruoxuan Xiong, Susan Athey, Mohsen Bayati, and Guido Imbens

source_refs.claim: Bai identifies the prognostic index as the offline design target but assumes that the index used for pairing is available before assignment.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai

open_problems.why_unsolved: The known-geometry capacity argument controls every accepted match through deterministic Hölder regularity. An estimated score is adapted to past assignments and outcomes, may be unavailable for recent units because of delay, and selects future pairs using noisy rankings. The first proof step that changes is the deterministic oscillation bound: it must be replaced by a uniform online prediction-error bound evaluated on adaptively selected reservoir pairs, while inference must account for outcome-to-design feedback.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An oracle inequality decomposing causal variance regret into the sharp hard-cap term and a matching upper-and-lower learning term depending on feedback delay and Hölder estimation error, accompanied by a studentized ATE limit theorem or exact conditional randomization test valid under the learned policy.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly frames why learning prognostic covariate importance during enrollment can improve power and identifies delayed responses as a practical boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: matching all covariates equally wastes reservoir capacity -> prior outcomes reveal prognostic geometry -> delayed feedback and a hard reservoir require an oracle learning-and-design guarantee

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize the variance-optimal prognostic index for matched-pair designs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It defines the oracle score and precision target against which learned online-pairing regret should be measured.

method_exemplars.technique: Use outcome-feedback sample splitting to retain asymptotic normality while early outcomes influence later design decisions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same feedback loop arises when earlier outcomes estimate the score used to form later reservoir pairs.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine online covariate-importance estimation, bootstrap distance thresholds, and rerandomization testing under the realized sequential algorithm.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the direct donor method, but the desired result must replace simulation evidence and rapid-response assumptions with delayed-feedback regret and validity guarantees.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend the hard-cap capacity/deadline frontier from opposite-treatment pairs to q-arm matched tuples in which each completed tuple receives every treatment once under a uniformly random orientation.

source_refs.claim: Kapelner and Krieger explicitly list adaptation of matching on the fly to experiments with more than two arms as future work.
source_refs.author: Adam Kapelner and Abba Krieger

source_refs.claim: Bai, Liu, and Tabord-Meehan establish estimation and inference for offline matched tuples and fully blocked factorial designs, not sequential tuple formation under a hard buffer.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai, Jizhou Liu, and Max Tabord-Meehan

source_refs.claim: Bugni, Canay, and Shaikh give corrected inference for multiple treatments under covariate-adaptive stratification but do not study online geometric tuple formation.
source_refs.author: Federico A. Bugni, Ivan A. Canay, and Azeem M. Shaikh

source_refs.claim: This work develops k-way online matching with delays through an H-metric and tree embedding, but its objective is not causal precision under finite capacity and a common deadline.
source_refs.author: Darya Melnyk, Yuyi Wang, and Roger Wattenhofer

open_problems.why_unsolved: The pairwise argument relies on parity and a scalar reservoir count, whereas q-arm tuples require controlling a vector of treatment deficits and cell residues modulo q during both ordinary operation and terminal clearing. Existing matched-tuples inference assumes blocks already exist, while k-way online matching uses delay costs and abstract subset metrics; neither identifies the capacity exponent or causal variance loss for sequential q-tuples.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax characterization of the T-, B-, beta-, d-, and q-dependent online matched-tuple regret, an implementable capped multiscale policy with forced terminal tuple completion, and a CLT with consistent covariance estimation for linear contrasts of the q average potential outcomes.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates matched tuples as the multi-treatment analogue of matched pairs and states the causal contrasts and inferential targets explicitly.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: multiple treatments require joint precision across contrasts -> homogeneous q-unit blocks allocate every arm once -> sequential enrollment with a finite reservoir requires an online tuple-capacity characterization

method_exemplars.technique: Define a k-point matching cost, embed its H-metric into a tree, and lift pair-matching delay analysis to k-way groups.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It identifies the first new proof object beyond pairs: a tuple cost and multiscale grouping argument that must be rebuilt for prognostic-score variance and a hard reservoir.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish joint asymptotic normality and consistent covariance estimation for linear contrasts under matched tuples.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the downstream limit theory once the online policy is shown to produce sufficiently homogeneous tuples.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply assignment-mechanism-specific variance correction for multiple-treatment covariate-adaptive randomization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Terminal tuple imbalances may resemble random stratum-level treatment fractions, making its correction strategy a natural robustness template.

literature_map:
Bai (2022, AER) identifies prognostic-index matched pairs as precision-optimal among stratified half-treatment designs, fixing the offline causal benchmark.
Kapelner and Krieger (2014, Biometrics) introduce matching on the fly: arrivals either match a randomized reservoir member or enter the randomized reservoir.
Kapelner and Krieger (2023, Biometrics) learn covariate importance, implement SeqExpMatch, and leave dynamic reservoir-dependent thresholds and multi-arm extensions open.
Chipman, Mayberry, and Greevy (2023, Statistics in Medicine) add batching, dynamic thresholds, and rematching without a hard-cap minimax frontier.
Zhao and Zhou (2024, Management Science) analyze a pigeonhole design for immediate online assignment; its geometry is relevant but it avoids a waiting reservoir and terminal clearing.
Bai, Romano, and Shaikh (2022, JASA) give matched-pair ATE limit theory and show familiar t procedures can be conservative.
Ma, Qin, Li, and Hu (2020, JASA) cover broad covariate-adaptive procedures, including pairwise sequential randomization, but not random matching blocks created under a cap.
Bugni, Canay, and Shaikh (2018, JASA) show that covariate-adaptive randomization can require assignment-specific variance corrections.
Ascher, Balkanski, Chatzitheodorou, and Gkatzelis (2026, EC) study arrivals joining or matching from a waiting pool, but impose no deterministic pool capacity or causal loss.
Kanoria (2025, Annals of Applied Probability) obtains dimension-dependent dynamic spatial-matching scaling using resources different from a finite experimental reservoir and deadline.
Mari, Pawlowski, Ren, and Sankowski (2023, AAMAS) study stochastic matching with delays and clearing penalties; delay prices are not hard occupancy constraints.
Gupta, Guruganesh, Peng, and Wajc (2019, ICALP) establish i.i.d.-versus-adversarial separations for one-sided stochastic online metric matching.
Azar, Chiplunkar, and Kaplan (2017, SODA) use tree embeddings and multiscale charging for matching with delays, a useful donor for clearance analysis but not a capacity theorem.
Bai, Liu, and Tabord-Meehan (2024, Quantitative Economics) provide estimation and inference for offline matched tuples, defining a multi-arm destination without online tuple formation.
Melnyk, Wang, and Wattenhofer (2021) extend delayed matching to k-way groups through H-metrics and tree embeddings; the missing bridge is hard capacity, a common deadline, and causal-precision loss.
